result.summary: Fixes an unhandled `std::bad_optional_access` exception when deserializing an assumeutxo snapshot on a custom signet with mismatched network magic. When constructing the error message, `SnapshotMetadata::Unserialize` now falls back to string "custom signet" if `GetNetworkForMagic` returns an empty optional for the node's network magic, and adds a unit test covering the scenario.
result.problem: When a node running on a custom signet attempts to load an assumeutxo snapshot from another network using `loadtxoutset`, building the network mismatch error throws `std::bad_optional_access` because custom signet magic bytes are not in the built-in network table. Instead of a helpful error describing the mismatch, the user receives an unhandled exception error.
evidence: PR description demonstrates the error output before and after: 'before: Unable to parse metadata: bad_optional_access' vs 'after: Unable to parse metadata: The network of the snapshot (main) does not match the network of this node (custom signet).'
The added unit test `snapshot_metadata_network_mismatch_custom_signet` reproduces the failure on master with `std::bad_optional_access`.
result.card: Prevents an unhandled std::bad_optional_access exception in loadtxoutset when loading a snapshot with mismatched network magic on a custom signet node. Because custom signet magic bytes are derived from the challenge rather than standard built-in networks, calling .value() on the node network lookup threw an exception while trying to construct the mismatch error message. The change provides a fallback label of custom signet when formatting the error and adds a unit test. Users on custom signets now receive a clean error message detailing the mismatch instead of a crash.

risk.why: A bug in this localized error message formatting would only alter the text of an error thrown when snapshot deserialization fails.
